day.text: Go ahead, I'm the Eagle now. I can't offer again this round, so the handshake is yours to offer. Meanwhile, Blair's phantom egg is our cat.

day.text: Finley shakes Casey's hand: they are bonded (Golden Wattle).

day.text: Confirmed: Finley is the Eagle, so the Frog story is true. Shaking. Everyone throw at Blair.
day.note: Sunflower confirms Finley is the Eagle, so Finley was the Frog and is Farm. Bond for +3. Then everyone throws at Blair.

day.text: My egg is real. Count it: two Eagle eggs, Ellis's egg, mine, maybe Gray's Frog egg. Casey should be +4 or +5. Nobody can verify Casey's Sunflower.

review.title: The Phantom Pigeon Egg
review.headline: An honest Pigeon's missing egg gets her eggsecuted while the lone cat banks 35.
review.summary: Drew was the only Meowfia, a Sphinx. Drew confused Alex the Kookaburra and then told one small lie, a Hawk claim. Blair truthfully said she laid an egg in Casey. Blair was secretly a Lazy Pigeon, so that egg actually went to Drew. Her claim clashed with Casey's correct egg math. Nobody considered the Lazy Pigeon, so the table read the mismatch as a lie. Sunflower checks and handshakes built a solid Farm bloc that threw 6 to 1 at Blair. Drew threw with that bloc and won 37 to 5.

rounds.recap: Casey's Eagle info, Gray's Galah claim and Ellis's Magpie report all fit together, and Finley's Frog claim was confirmed by Sunflower. That left Blair's Pigeon egg as the one claim that didn't fit. It didn't fit because Blair was unknowingly a Lazy Pigeon, so the egg went to Drew instead. Drew claimed Hawk, nobody pressed him, and he joined the pile-on. Farm eggsecuted one of its own, and Drew banked 35.

highlights.text: Casey named Alex as Drew's visitor before Alex claimed anything, which proved Casey's Eagle story without any extra checks.
Finley paid an egg to extend the day after CAW CAW, claimed Frog, and got that claim confirmed by Casey's Sunflower check.
Blair argued that Casey should be at +4 or +5. It was the right instinct, but her egg had gone to Drew, so it pointed at the wrong player.
Drew's whole lie was one line, a Hawk claim saying he visited Alex. That one line explained Alex's confusion and steered the table onto Blair and Finley.

confusions.what: Gray kept S8 in the throw because it 'comes back if we lose'. That can't happen: Farm only loses here if Blair is Farm, and throwing at your own team gets no consolation card.
Casey called Blair a liar and never considered the Lazy Pigeon. It was in the pool, and it explains exactly where Blair's egg went.
Finley said 'I can't offer again this round.' No rule limits handshake offers.
Ellis kept C1 because it is 'worth more kept'. A 1 is worth 1 whether you keep it or bank it.
Blair believed she was the Pigeon, as the card intends. Her egg math was honest but wrong, and it led her to throw at Casey, a teammate.

worked: The Lazy Pigeon made the whole round. One honest claim became the only 'contradiction' on the table, and an innocent player died for it. That is great drama, but nobody even named the card as a possible explanation. Consider a reminder in the app, or a rule that a Pigeon claim invites a Lazy Pigeon check.

Golden Wattle gave Farm its only points (+3 per bonded pair). Handshakes worked as public trust signals, but they were offered on thin evidence. Sunflower worked well: one private check confirmed Finley and set up a bond.
problems: Through the Sphinx's list of Farm roles in play, Drew deduced he was the only Meowfia. Knowing he had no partners let him throw everything with the majority. That may be too much information for one cat.

A lone cat who joins the bandwagon banks every card it throws. The result was 37 to 5 in a one-round game. Consider capping the cat's payout or scaling it by the number of Meowfia. As it stands, one wrong vote decides the whole game.

Drew's Hawk claim was never tested. Drew gained 2 eggs and never gave his count. Ellis's Magpie report had already put Drew in play, but nobody followed up. A shorter day under Mulberry and early CAW CAW calls cut off follow-up questions. Look at whether CAW CAW opening at 50% ends the day too fast.
